It was the soundtrack of the show that heightened a feeling of a haunted or healing home, heard through Kim Gordon’s unmistakable voice. Bellotti approaches the house from the perspective of a home, treated as an emotional sanctuary where one either belongs or feels the urge to flee. This sophomore collection thrives on the tension of a lived-in space, filled with both calm and internal contradiction. The creative director draws on a very personal history for this vision, noting that his father worked as an upholsterer. This familiarity with the textures of a domestic interior allows him to treat fabric like furniture, moving codes and tropes around with a playful lack of ceremony.
